questions.stem: State the event that defines sexual reproduction.
questions.modelAnswer: Sexual reproduction means offspring arise from the fusion of a male and a female gamete.

questions.stem: Name the two types of cell division involved in sexual reproduction and their roles.
questions.modelAnswer: Meiosis halves the chromosome number to produce gametes, and mitosis divides the zygote as it develops into an embryo.

questions.stem: Explain why offspring of sexual reproduction are genetically unique.
questions.modelAnswer: Each offspring inherits genetic material from both parents, and meiosis plus fertilisation recombine it, so no offspring matches either parent's genome.

questions.stem: A population faces a new disease. Explain why its sexually produced members give the species an edge.
questions.modelAnswer: Sexual reproduction has introduced variation, so some individuals carry gene combinations that resist the disease and can survive to reproduce.

questions.stem: State what asexual reproduction produces from a single parent.
questions.modelAnswer: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are genetically identical clones of the single parent.

questions.stem: State the cost of asexual reproduction's lack of variation.
questions.modelAnswer: With nothing to vary, a population faces disease or environmental change far more exposed.

questions.stem: Explain why no fertilisation occurs in asexual reproduction.
questions.modelAnswer: One parent cell alone is enough, so no second gamete arrives and nothing mixes.

questions.stem: A greenhouse grower relies on cloned cuttings. State one benefit and one risk of that choice.
questions.modelAnswer: The benefit is fast, efficient production of identical plants, and the risk is that a single disease could sweep every clone since none vary genetically.

questions.stem: State the number of parent cells in each reproduction mode.
questions.modelAnswer: Asexual reproduction uses one parent cell and sexual reproduction uses two.

questions.stem: State the genetic similarity of offspring in each mode.
questions.modelAnswer: Asexual offspring are genetically identical clones, while sexual offspring are genetically unique and different from both parents.

questions.stem: Explain why the division row of the comparison table mentions both meiosis and mitosis for sexual reproduction.
questions.modelAnswer: Meiosis first produces the haploid gametes, and after fertilisation mitosis divides the zygote as it grows into an embryo, so both divisions appear in the sexual column.

questions.stem: Complete a three-row comparison for bacteria dividing by copying versus flowering plants pairing by gametes.
questions.modelAnswer: The bacterial route matches asexual reproduction with one parent, mitotic copying and identical offspring, while the plant route matches sexual reproduction with two parents, meiosis then mitosis and unique offspring.
